output.model_sql:
SELECT product_id, category, list_price,
       CASE WHEN list_price < 50 THEN 'budget'
            WHEN list_price < 200 THEN 'mid'
            ELSE 'premium' END AS price_band
FROM {{ source('raw', 'products') }}
WHERE is_active
output.notes: Direct one-to-one translation. The source reference was swapped for source('raw','products'). Column order is the same as the legacy job: product_id, category, list_price, price_band. There are no post-CREATE statements to fold in. This assumes is_active is a BOOLEAN column in DuckDB. If it lands as an integer or string, the bare WHERE predicate may behave differently or fail, so check the source type.
quirks_found: A NULL list_price fails both comparisons and falls through to ELSE, so it is labelled 'premium'.
Band boundaries are exclusive on the upper end: a price of exactly 50 is 'mid' and exactly 200 is 'premium'.
WHERE is_active silently drops rows where is_active is NULL, not just rows where it is false.
No deduplication on product_id. Duplicate product rows in raw.products pass straight through to the dimension.
Negative list_price values are labelled 'budget' with no validation.
